description: Curated MiniC programs served by GET /api/examples. Every file named here is loaded from disk on request; nothing is inlined, so the directory a reader browses and the programs the compiler tests are the same files.

examples.name: hello
examples.title: Hello, world
examples.summary: The smallest complete program: one print and a return value.

examples.name: arithmetic
examples.title: Arithmetic and promotion
examples.summary: Integer and float arithmetic side by side, including the implicit int to float promotion.

examples.name: loops
examples.title: while and for
examples.summary: The same sum written twice. Produces the back edges the CFG and the data-flow stepper need.

examples.name: short-circuit
examples.title: Short-circuit evaluation
examples.summary: The right operand of && and || is only read when it has to be. A constant condition on the left makes one side of a branch unreachable.

examples.name: recursion
examples.title: Recursion
examples.summary: Factorial, Fibonacci, and an if/else-if chain. The deepest call graph in the corpus, and the one the step limit is sized for.

examples.name: io
examples.title: Reading input
examples.summary: scanf and printf with several specifiers in one string. The only example that needs stdin, and the one whose read results are never used.

examples.name: sugar-and-loops
examples.title: Assignment sugar, break, continue
examples.summary: Compound assignment and increments lowered away, plus break and continue in one loop body.

examples.name: mixed-types
examples.title: Mixed int and float
examples.summary: Promotion, narrowing, and float comparisons. The case where a view that assumes every value is an int falls over.

examples.name: sorting
examples.title: Sorting three values
examples.summary: The largest example: seven functions, comparison helpers, swaps on locals, and a gcd loop.

examples.name: unreachable
examples.title: Unreachable code
examples.summary: Code after a return, and a return inside a loop. The corpus's end-to-end test for structural versus conditional unreachability.

examples.name: dead-assignments
examples.title: Dead assignments
examples.summary: Writes that are overwritten before any read, and a loop-local that is never used. What the dead-store pass removes.

examples.name: constant-folding
examples.title: Constant folding
examples.summary: Expressions built entirely from literals, which the compiler evaluates without running anything.

examples.name: constant-propagation
examples.title: Constant propagation
examples.summary: Variables assigned a literal and never written again, plus a loop-local that must not be propagated.

examples.name: use-before-init
examples.title: Read before assignment
examples.summary: A local declared with no value, read anyway. Reaching definitions prove the read has no definition at all.

examples.name: division-by-zero
examples.title: Division by a literal zero
examples.summary: Valid MiniC that always aborts. The case that proves the dead-code analysis refuses to delete a statement whose only effect is a guaranteed failure.

examples.name: undeclared-identifier
examples.title: Undeclared identifier
examples.summary: Reads a name that was never declared.

examples.name: type-mismatch
examples.title: Return type mismatch
examples.summary: An int function returning a string literal.

examples.name: missing-semicolon
examples.title: Missing semicolon
examples.summary: A statement that is not terminated, so the parser recovers and reports the next one too.

examples.name: redeclared-local
examples.title: Redeclared local
examples.summary: Two declarations of the same name in one scope.

examples.name: wrong-arity
examples.title: Wrong argument count
examples.summary: A call with more arguments than the declaration accepts.

examples.name: break-outside-loop
examples.title: break outside a loop
examples.summary: break and continue used where no loop encloses them.

examples.name: unterminated-string
examples.title: Unterminated string
examples.summary: A string literal with no closing quote.

examples.name: format-count-mismatch
examples.title: Too few arguments
examples.summary: A format string with more specifiers than arguments.

examples.name: void-value
examples.title: Using a void value
examples.summary: Initialising a variable from a function that returns nothing.

examples.name: format-type-mismatch
examples.title: Format specifier type mismatch
examples.summary: A %f specifier supplied with an int argument.

examples.name: lone-pipe
examples.title: A single pipe
examples.summary: `|` where `||` was meant. Guessing would be worse than saying so.

examples.name: preprocessor-directive
examples.title: Preprocessor directive
examples.summary: An #include. MiniC has no headers; printf and scanf are built in.

examples.name: unterminated-comment
examples.title: Unterminated comment
examples.summary: A block comment with no closing marker, so the rest of the file is comment.

examples.name: undeclared-function
examples.title: Undeclared function
examples.summary: A call to a function that does not exist. MiniC has no implicit declarations, so a typo is an error here rather than a link-time surprise.
